title: Password reset and authentication flow security: detect predictable tokens, token reuse, and reset poisoning
goal: WebGoat has passwordreset and insecurelogin modules. These authentication flow flaws are not covered by any current runner. Implement an auth-flow runner: (1) Password Reset Token Predictability: trigger password reset for a test account, collect 5 reset tokens over time, analyse for: sequential patterns (token increments), timestamp-based tokens, short length (<128 bits), tokens that don't expire. (2) Password Reset Token Reuse: verify that a used reset token cannot be reused. (3) Host Header Injection in Password Reset: send password reset request with a forged Host header pointing to an attacker-controlled domain. If the reset link in the email uses the Host header value → Host Header Injection leading to account takeover. (4) Username Enumeration: compare response time and content for valid vs invalid usernames on login/reset forms. Timing differences or different error messages → Username Enumeration. (5) Brute Force Protection: attempt 10 consecutive failed logins. Check if account lockout triggers or rate limiting applies. No lockout → Brute Force vulnerability. (6) Insecure Login (credentials in GET params or HTTP): detect login forms submitting credentials over HTTP or via GET parameters (appear in server logs). Active tier, requires configured test account credentials.
scope: WebGoat passwordreset + insecurelogin modules. Current coverage: ❌ Not implemented. Authentication flow flaws are consistently in the top 5 findings in real pentest engagements.
